key_insight: Real-time, on‑the‑fly agent synthesis bypasses core software engineering practices; the paper introduces an "AI Workflow Store" to reintroduce iterative design, testing, and staged deployment so personal agents become robust and auditable.
problem_solved: Current agent paradigms prioritize immediate plan synthesis and execution, which short‑circuit disciplined SE processes and produce brittle, unpredictable, and hard‑to‑govern personal agents.
method: Define an AI Workflow Store: a catalog of reusable agent workflows, artifacts, and checkpoints that codify design, tests, and deployment gates.
Integrate SE practices into agent lifecycles: automated unit/integration/adversarial tests, versioning, staged rollouts, and post‑deploy monitoring for agents.
Provide tooling and orchestration to compose, evaluate, and iterate on agent behaviors outside the strict real‑time loop, enabling repeatable experiments and controlled deployments.
impact: Bringing classical SE controls to agent development reduces failures, increases reproducibility and safety, and lets ML/engineering teams deploy personal agents with measurable reliability and governance.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side diagram: "On‑the‑fly loop" vs "Workflow‑driven lifecycle" showing missing SE steps in the first and inserted stages (test, adversarial eval, staging) in the second.
Pipeline infographic of the AI Workflow Store: catalog → compose → test (unit/adversarial) → stage → monitor, with icons for each stage.
Chart showing expected benefits: fewer runtime failures, faster rollback, higher test coverage (conceptual bars or adoption metrics).
Icon set: workflow catalog, test shield, deployment gate, observability/monitoring dashboard to communicate governance and safety.
paper_title: Engineering Robustness into Personal Agents with the AI Workflow Store
paper_authors: Roxana Geambasu, Mariana Raykova, Pierre Tholoniat, Trishita Tiwari, Lillian Tsai
